  because both are often fast. The guarantee is the changed fact.
- Do not update the base card from one surprising run. Verify the new
  rule, then correct the prerequisite or breaker with evidence.
- Do not copy replacement implementations into the packet. Multiple
  owners drift in arithmetic, ties, mutation, and error behavior.
- Stop a packet after its bounded evidence is complete. Interesting
  follow-up changes belong in separately scheduled forks.

##### When to choose it

Use controlled variations after a base family passes its readiness
gate but before marking transfer complete. They are especially useful
when a method depends on ordering, signs, uniqueness, graph weights,
mutation, online arrival, tie rules, or a particular resource bound.

Choose a variation whose changed fact appears in the base card's
preconditions or breaker. Prefer the smallest input that makes the
affected decision observable. Include both a variation where the
method survives and one where it fails, so practice does not teach
that every wording change demands a new algorithm.

Use ordinary regression tests when only values change inside the old
contract. Use a composed challenge after independent forks pass. Use
a new family card when the changed contract requires a different
state meaning and invariant rather than a local adaptation.

Do not use variations to guess arbitrary interview puzzles. Start
from in-scope contracts and real proof boundaries. When a role adds a
specialized capability, apply the [advanced-topic audit](
#c162-advanced-and-specialized-interview-topics) before investing in
a new owner.

For the walkthrough's algorithms, study the
[variable sliding window](
#b52-variable-sliding-window-map-or-counters),
[signed shortest-range owner](
#b57-shortest-signed-sum-range-prefix-sums-and-deque), and
[negative-value diagnostic](
#c141-why-negative-values-can-break-a-sliding-window). Then record
mistakes by the exact state definition or invariant that failed in
the next lesson.

#### C.16.4 Track mistakes by invariant and state definition

##### Problem and contract

A list such as "binary search wrong" or "careless off-by-one" does
not say what belief should change. Logging every wrong output also
overcounts one early defect when it causes many later symptoms.

This lesson builds a mistake index from reproducible attempt evidence.
Its inputs are:

- the exact contract and owner used by the attempt;
- the input, expected result, and observed result;
- an implementation or sufficiently exact transition trace;
- whether notes, hints, or an oracle were used; and
- a finite number K of review units available now.

A review unit is one bounded correction, closed-notes reproduction,
or transfer check. It is not a promise that every record will be
resolved in one sitting.

The output is an index of mistake records grouped by the missing state
meaning, invariant clause, proof fact, or contract fact. Each record
contains:

```text
attempt evidence     input, expected result, observed result, help
first divergence     earliest unsupported decision or state
state meaning        what each relevant value or region should mean
required fact        invariant, precondition, transition, or bound
branch signature     the exact branch that lost the fact
small case           minimized valid reproducer and nearby pass
correction           changed belief, not only changed syntax
evidence state       what has been reproduced without notes
next action          one bounded check that can advance the state
```

Record one first divergence from a run. After correcting it, rerun
from the beginning. If another independent defect then appears, give
that defect its own record. Do not create separate records for every
wrong state downstream of the same first divergence.

Not every failure is an invariant failure. Use the nearest honest
owner:

```text
contract or precondition   misunderstood valid input or output
state definition           stored value or boundary had no exact role
invariant or transition    a branch lost a required fact
progress or termination    no bounded measure strictly advanced
resource guarantee         result was right but budget was missed
language or tooling        method was clear but expression was not
```

A language error should not be relabeled as an algorithm failure, and
a wrong algorithm choice should not be hidden as a typo. Both can be
tracked, but they need different corrections.

Read [state meanings, invariants, and termination](
#c101-state-meanings-invariants-and-termination) for the proof
obligations and [counterexamples](
#c102-counterexamples-and-adversarial-inputs) for first divergence
and minimization. The [core portfolio](
#c161-core-structures-and-reusable-algorithm-families) owns readiness
decisions. This lesson owns the evidence record that feeds them.

##### Mental model

Turn a failed attempt into a short causal chain:

```text
attempt
    -> normalize contract and expected result
        -> replay expected and observed state together
            -> stop at first divergence
                -> name the missing fact
                    -> shrink and preserve the case
                        -> correct, replay, and transfer
```

The first divergence is the earliest point where the actual state no
longer supports the contract. The final wrong answer is evidence that
something failed; the first divergence identifies what to practice.

Keep these levels separate:

```text
state role       right is the exclusive candidate boundary
invariant        the true lower bound remains in [left,right]
transition       a qualifying middle sets right=middle
progress         right-left strictly decreases while positive
postcondition    exit boundary is the first qualifying position
```

A useful bucket key is:

```text
owner / state role / required invariant or proof fact
```

Keep the exact branch as a signature inside the bucket. Two lower
bound failures may both lose answer containment, while one discards a
qualifying middle and another classifies equality as too small. They
belong to the same invariant bucket but remain distinct regressions.

Use evidence states rather than a confidence score:

```text
open              failure reproduced; correction not yet replayed
corrected once    corrected trace or code passed with sources open
reproduced cold   same case passed later without solution notes
transfer shown    independent case or story used the same fact
regressed         a later cold check failed; record is open again
```

Reading a solution does not advance the state. A passing run with the
solution visible can establish `corrected once`, but only a later
closed-notes run can establish `reproduced cold`.

Choose next actions with ordered evidence gates, not invented points:

1. repair an open prerequisite that blocks current in-scope work;
2. repair a bucket repeated across independent attempts;
3. reproduce a correction that has not passed cold;
4. test transfer where only the original problem has passed; and
5. leave a transferred record dormant until new failure evidence.

When two records meet the same gate, prefer the one needed by the
next accepted practice unit. A global numeric severity score would
hide those actual dependencies.

##### Worked walkthrough

A learner has four attempt reports and K=3 review units:

```text
A  lower bound [1,3], target 3: expected 1, observed 0
B  lower bound [2,2,2], target 2: expected 0, observed 3
C  shortest sum [2,-1,2,1], target 3: expected 2, observed 3
D  BFS diamond 0->[1,2], 1->[3], 2->[3]: vertex 3 queued twice
```

A and B were independent closed-notes attempts. C used no hint but
chose the positive-only window. D marked graph vertices when removed
from the queue instead of when appended. The next accepted practice
unit uses signed ranges; graph practice follows later.

Expected result: create three diagnostic buckets, preserve two branch
signatures in the lower-bound bucket, spend two units repairing and
transferring that repeated prerequisite, spend one unit correcting
the signed-window selection, and leave the BFS record open with an
exact next action.

Initial state: the mistake index is empty, all four reports are
unclassified, K is 3, and no evidence state has been awarded.

1. Decision: normalize report A against the lower-bound contract.
   The true boundary B is 1. With `left=0`, `right=2`, middle 1
   qualifies. The flawed update uses `right=middle-1`, producing
   `[0,0)` instead of retaining middle with `right=middle`.
   After: A stops at the first divergence, actual right 0 versus
   required right 1; the later wrong return is not logged separately.
   Known correct: the update excludes B=1 and violates answer
   containment before any exit reasoning occurs.
2. Decision: create the key `lower-bound / candidate boundaries /
   B remains in [left,right]`. Store A's branch signature as
   `qualifying middle incorrectly subtracts one` and preserve
   `[1,3]`, target 3, as its small regression.
   After: the lower-bound bucket has one open record and no correction
   evidence.
   Known correct: the label names the lost fact and state role rather
   than the surface symptom "off by one."
3. Decision: replay report B. With `left=0`, `right=3`, true B is 0
   and middle 1 equals the target. The flawed equality branch treats
   middle as too small and sets `left=middle+1`, immediately making
   `left=2 > B=0`.
   After: add a second signature, `equality moves left`, to the same
   answer-containment bucket; its evidence count is two attempts.
   Known correct: A and B use different erroneous branches but lose
   the same invariant clause on independent inputs.
4. Decision: classify report C. The positive-window trace first
   records length 3. At the final state `[1,4)`, sum 2 is below
   target, so it refuses to shrink; removing left value -1 would
   raise the sum to 3 and expose `[2,4)`, length 2.
   After: create `signed threshold window / boundary effect /
   shrinking below target cannot help` with state `open`.
   Known correct: the failure is a violated precondition and decision
   fact, not an arithmetic or pointer-syntax error.
5. Decision: classify report D using the BFS owner. After scanning
   vertex 1, vertex 3 is pending but unmarked. When vertex 2 scans
   edge `2 -> 3`, it sees 3 as undiscovered and appends it again.
   After: create `BFS / discovered state / each queued vertex is
   already discovered`, with `mark on dequeue` as the branch
   signature and the four-vertex diamond as its regression.
   Known correct: the first divergence is leaving 3 unmarked after
   its first append; the duplicate queue entry is the later symptom.
6. Decision: apply the review gates. The lower-bound bucket is a core
   prerequisite and has repeated independent evidence. Allocate unit
   1 to correction and unit 2 to cold transfer. Allocate unit 3 to
   the signed-window method-selection failure. K becomes zero.
   After: BFS stays open with next action `mark before enqueue, then
   replay the diamond`; it is not deleted or mislabeled ready.
   Known correct: all allocation follows explicit scope, dependency,
   recurrence, and evidence facts rather than a numeric score.
7. Decision: execute lower-bound unit 1 with C.10.1 open. State the
   three regions, replay both faulty branches, and use
   `right=middle` for a qualifying middle while equality remains in
   the not-smaller branch.
   After: both saved regressions return their expected boundaries;
   the bucket advances to `corrected once` and unit 1 is consumed.
   Known correct: source-assisted correction is evidence of a fixed
   trace, not yet evidence of independent recall.
8. Decision: close the source for unit 2. First replay A and B cold.
   Then solve an independent search-insertion prompt on `[1,2,2,4]`
   with target 3 and return boundary 3. Explain why a qualifying
   middle is retained and why width strictly decreases.
   After: the bucket advances through `reproduced cold` to
   `transfer shown`; unit 2 is consumed.
   Known correct: a new input used the same containment invariant and
   both transition and termination facts without notes.
9. Decision: use unit 3 on report C. Write the nonnegative boundary
   effects, refute them with -1, then replay the prefix/deque owner on
   `[2,-1,2,1]` to obtain length 2.
   After: the signed-window bucket becomes `corrected once`; unit 3
   is consumed and K is zero.
   Known correct: the corrected selection has been traced, but cold
   reproduction and transfer remain explicit next actions.
10. Decision: K is zero, so stop and return the index, evidence
    states, preserved regressions, and unscheduled next actions.
    After: lower bound is `transfer shown`; signed window is
    `corrected once`; BFS remains `open`.
    Known correct: exhausted budget has not been mistaken for mastery
    or used to erase unresolved evidence.

Focused non-algorithm case: if the learner can state the heap
invariant but cannot write Go's `heap.Interface` methods, record a
language or tooling gap linked to the heap owner. Repeating a heap
proof will not repair the missing interface fluency.

Focused downstream case: a bad binary-search boundary may later cause
an out-of-range read. Log the first boundary divergence. Add a second
record only if the read remains unsafe after the boundary update is
corrected.

Focused surprising-pass case: if an implementation returns the right
value but its trace violates the invariant, keep the record. One input
can pass accidentally; the unsupported decision still needs a breaker
or cross-check.

Nearby passing controls keep each branch diagnosis honest. The flawed
A update can still return 2 for `[1,3]`, target 4, because its bad
qualifying branch is never used. B's equality defect is not reached by
`[1,3]`, target 2. The positive window succeeds on `[2,1]`, target 3,
and a graph with only one path to each vertex hides mark-on-dequeue.

##### Implementation

Keep mistake records beside the family cards from C.16.1. A plain
Markdown file, issue tracker, or structured note is sufficient when
it preserves the fields and links. Use this template:

```text
record ID:
family card and primary owner:
attempt context and help used:
contract and preconditions:
input, expected result, observed result:
first divergent decision and state:
state meanings at that program point:
required invariant, proof fact, or resource bound:
bucket key and branch signature:
small failing case and nearby passing case:
correction in words:
regression or oracle link:
evidence state:
next bounded action:
later evidence and regressions:
```

Create or update a record in this order:

1. Freeze the contract and independently establish the expected
   result.
2. Replay actual and expected state from the same initial state.
3. Stop at the first divergent decision.
4. Write every relevant state value as a sentence.
5. Name the first lost invariant, precondition, progress fact, or
   resource guarantee.
6. Minimize the case without changing the failure predicate.
7. Attach the record to an existing bucket or create an exact key.
8. Write one correction and one bounded next action.
9. Preserve a regression in the executable owner when practical.
10. Append later evidence; do not rewrite assisted work as cold work.

Link implementations and proofs instead of copying them. The
[lower-bound proof owner](
#c101-state-meanings-invariants-and-termination),
[signed-window diagnostic](
#c141-why-negative-values-can-break-a-sliding-window), and
[graph BFS owner](
#b122-breadth-first-search-adjacency-list-and-queue) contain the
complete reasoning used by the walkthrough.

When code owns the defect, add the minimized reproducer to that
owner's test home. Record its path or test name, not a pasted copy of
the implementation. Use [brute-force cross-checking](
#c104-cross-check-optimized-code-against-brute-force) when a small
independent oracle can establish expected results across a bounded
domain.

Keep an append-only evidence history inside each record. A later cold
failure changes `transfer shown` to `regressed`; it does not delete
the earlier success. The sequence explains whether the skill was
learned, retained, and then lost.

Do not automate evidence state from accepted submissions, elapsed
time, or file completion. Tools can attach test output and timestamps,
but assisted versus cold execution and the explained invariant remain
human-observed facts.

##### Why it works

A deterministic replay has one earliest state where actual execution
stops matching the required reasoning. Every later wrong state depends
on that divergence or on another defect not yet exposed. Recording the
first divergence therefore avoids treating one cause as many mistakes.
Rerunning after correction reveals whether another independent cause
exists.

State meanings localize the missing knowledge. If `right` is merely
remembered as "an index," `right=middle-1` may look plausible. Reading
it as the exclusive boundary of the unresolved interval makes the
lost candidate visible before code runs.

Invariant buckets support transfer. Problem titles and sample values
change, but the claim "the true boundary remains in [left,right]" is
the same in search insertion and first-occurrence tasks. Distinct
branch signatures prevent that useful grouping from erasing the exact
transition that failed.

Evidence states prevent recognition from being called mastery. A
correction with the source open shows that the repaired explanation
can be followed. Cold reproduction shows recall on the saved case. An
independent variation shows that the state and invariant, rather than
only the original code shape, were retrieved.

The priority gates are justified by current work. A blocking
prerequisite prevents later practice from being interpreted. Repeated
independent failures are stronger evidence of a stable gap than one
incident. A corrected-but-not-cold record has not passed the readiness
gate. A transferred record needs no new unit without contrary
evidence.

The process terminates for one planning cycle. There are finitely many
attempt reports and K is finite. Each report is classified once, and
each executed review unit decreases K. A newly revealed defect is
queued for a later bounded action rather than starting an unlimited
repair loop.

The index does not prove general competence. It preserves evidence
about observed attempts. Untested families, composed changes, time
pressure, and language fluency can still reveal new gaps.

##### Costs and tradeoffs

Let A be the number of attempt reports, S the total number of traced
transitions, M the number of retained mistake records, B the number
of buckets, and K the available review units.

Replaying attempts to first divergence takes O(S) diagnostic work.
Minimization adds the cost of rerunning each tried reduction; it
depends on the input shape and failure predicate rather than A alone.

With a map from bucket key to records, inserting M records takes
expected O(M) map work and O(M+B) retained index storage, plus the
size of saved traces and test cases. A sorted text index can use
O(M log M) organization work without expected hash timing.

A simple priority pass over B buckets for each of K units takes
O(K*B) planning work. Human practice dominates that bookkeeping. If
unit I uses `correct[I]`, `replay[I]`, and `transfer[I]` time, total
study time is their sum over the executed units.

A minimized regression reduces routine test cost and makes the proof
hinge visible. Exhaustive or brute-force oracles may add polynomial or
exponential test work over a bounded domain; their owners must state
those limits separately.

Detailed records cost attention. Log failures that change a contract,
state meaning, invariant, transition, progress fact, or resource
choice. A spelling correction that is immediately obvious may need no
permanent record unless it repeats or exposes a tooling gap.

Over-grouping makes the index vague; under-grouping hides recurrence.
The stable invariant bucket plus exact branch signatures balances both
risks. Revisit a key when its records require different corrections.

##### Edge cases and mistakes

- With K=0, classify new evidence and retain next actions, but award
  no correction, cold-replay, or transfer state.
- No records does not prove no gaps. It may mean no cold attempt has
  been observed. Preserve successful readiness evidence too.
- An ambiguous contract cannot produce a trustworthy mistake record.
  Resolve valid input, output, ties, and ownership before diagnosis.
- An invalid input is not a counterexample to a theorem that excludes
  it. Track missing validation against the boundary contract instead.
- Derive the expected result independently. A flawed implementation
  cannot serve as its own oracle.
- Record the first divergence, not the loudest symptom. A final panic
  may follow several steps after candidate containment was lost.
- After fixing the first divergence, rerun from the initial state.
  Only then can a later failure justify another record.
- Do not write "off by one" without naming the interval convention,
  boundary role, lost candidate, and wrong branch.
- Do not write "forgot visited." State whether visited means
  discovered or fully processed and when that fact becomes true.
- Two records sharing a title may need different buckets. Wrong
  equality classification and missing progress can require different
  corrections even inside binary search.
- Two different stories may share a bucket. Search insertion and
  first occurrence can lose the same answer-containment invariant.
- A compiler error is language evidence unless the syntax failure
  came from an undefined state design. Diagnose the earliest gap.
- A correct output can still violate mutation, tie, complexity, or
  termination guarantees. Compare every observable contract field.
- A hint-assisted pass is not cold reproduction. Retain the help field
  instead of upgrading evidence from memory.
- One cold pass on the original case is not transfer. Use a different
  valid input, story, or nonessential representation.
- A later failure does not erase earlier evidence. Mark `regressed`,
  append the new divergence, and choose another bounded action.
- A nondeterministic failure needs a replayable seed, operation order,
  or schedule. Without one, the first divergence remains unverified.
- Do not close a record because K reached zero. Preserve its current
  state and next executable step.
- Do not rank by shame, difficulty labels, or invented frequency.
  Use current scope, prerequisites, recurrence, and evidence state.
- Do not paste full solutions into the log. Link the primary owner so
  fixes to contracts, arithmetic, and ties remain synchronized.
- A timestamp shows when evidence occurred, not whether it is still
  retained. Only a later cold check supplies retention evidence.

##### When to choose it

Create or update a record after a failed or hint-assisted attempt, an
unexpected pass with unsupported reasoning, a violated resource bound,
or a breaker that changes the selected method. Use the index before
allocating the next review units so practice repairs observed gaps.

Use invariant buckets for recurring algorithm reasoning. Use contract,
resource, or language buckets when those are the actual owners. Keep
the same evidence states so assisted correction, cold recall,
transfer, and regression remain distinguishable.

Do not maintain a detailed record for every immediately corrected
keystroke. Promote it when it repeats, changes observable behavior, or
reveals missing language fluency. Do not use the log as a substitute
for executing tests, proving a method, or practicing without notes.

Use [C.10.1](#c101-state-meanings-invariants-and-termination) to
write the missing fact, [C.10.2](
#c102-counterexamples-and-adversarial-inputs) to minimize and preserve
the failure, and [C.10.4](
#c104-cross-check-optimized-code-against-brute-force) when an oracle
can compare bounded inputs. Feed the resulting evidence back into the
[core portfolio](
#c161-core-structures-and-reusable-algorithm-families) and use
[controlled variations](
#c163-practice-variations-that-change-one-assumption) for transfer.
